title: Songkhla 3 Days 2 Nights — Old Town, Koh Yo & Hat Yai | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A relaxed 3-day Songkhla itinerary in southern Thailand: Old Town's Nang Ngam Road, Khao Tang Kuan, Koh Yo lakeside seafood, and Hat Yai markets — with hours, fees, and local spots.
keywords: Songkhla 3 days 2 nights, Songkhla itinerary, Songkhla old town, Koh Yo, Hat Yai, Nang Ngam Road
h1:
Songkhla 3 Days 2 Nights
Old Town, Koh Yo, Hat Yai
intro: Most people fly into Hat Yai and never leave the city, yet drive just another 30 minutes and you hit Songkhla's old town — a lakeside quarter with a completely different vibe. This 3-day plan strings three zones together: Day 1 exploring the old town and Samila Beach, Day 2 crossing the bridge to Koh Yo for lakeside seafood, then saving the last day for eating and shopping your way through Hat Yai before the flight home. Every spot in this plan has been checked for opening hours and entry fees.

blocks.html: Songkhla and Hat Yai are in different districts, about 30 km apart — roughly 30–40 minutes by car. Most visitors land at Hat Yai International Airport and then decide which side to base in. We'd suggest staying two nights in Songkhla's old-town area so you can explore at a relaxed pace, then moving to Hat Yai on the last night to be close to the airport. If switching hotels feels like a hassle, staying in Hat Yai the whole time and driving out each day works too — the distance really isn't far.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Songkhla Old Town & Samila Beach

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Walk Nang Ngam Road, climb Khao Tang Kuan, then wind down at Samila Beach

items.activity: Land at Hat Yai Airport, pick up a rental car or take transport into Songkhla city, then check into your hotel near the old town or Samila Beach
items.note: Hat Yai Airport to Songkhla city takes about 35–40 min · A rental car is the most flexible option since attractions are spread across multiple zones

items.activity: Start exploring the old town along three parallel streets — Nakhon Nok, Nakhon Nai, and Nang Ngam — taking in the Sino-Portuguese shophouses and street art tucked into the lanes
items.note: Nang Ngam Road has the most food and cafés — you can walk the whole length stopping to snap photos · Parking is scarce on weekends; arriving mid-morning gives you a better chance of finding a spot

items.activity: Lunch on Nang Ngam Road — try the old-school clay-pot ice cream, Pa Mol's charcoal egg cakes, and browse the small snack stalls along the way
items.note: Pa Mol's egg cakes and the clay-pot ice cream are the street's signatures, priced in the tens of baht · Some popular stalls sell out before afternoon

items.activity: Head up Khao Tang Kuan for a 360-degree view over Songkhla city and the lake, and pay respects at the hilltop Phra That Chedi Luang
items.note: The elevator runs 08:30–17:30, adult THB 30, child THB 20 · You can also climb the steps if you prefer

items.activity: Make your way down to Samila Beach — photograph the city's Golden Mermaid statue and the cat-and-rat sculptures, then stroll along the shore in the sea breeze
items.note: Late afternoon is the best time: the sun is softer and the sea breeze picks up · Several seafood restaurants line the beach road if you want to sit a while

items.activity: Dinner at a seafood restaurant on Samila Beach, or head back into town to eat in the old-town district
items.note: A string of casual seafood places sit along the Samila waterfront — the evening atmosphere is easygoing with views out to sea

blocks.title: Day 1 Tip
blocks.html: The old town and Samila Beach are only a few kilometres apart — 5–10 min by car. Plan old-town walking for the late morning, duck into a café to avoid the midday heat, then head to Khao Tang Kuan and the beach in the late afternoon. You get the best light and it's not nearly as hot.

blocks.text: Cafés and Stops in the Old Town

blocks.html: When the midday sun gets fierce, the old-town quarter has plenty of atmospheric cafés inside renovated Sino-Portuguese shophouses where you can rest your feet. The interiors carry the feel of an old trading port — a good spot to sit with a coffee before walking on.

items.name: Tai Tun Café
items.blurb: A newer toast café in a vintage shophouse on the Nang Ngam strip — thick-cut toast with generous toppings, cool interior, perfect for escaping the afternoon heat

items.name: Yap Ian Choi Library
items.blurb: A lovingly preserved old building in the heart of the old town converted into a reading space and hangout — step inside to admire the architecture and cool off for free

items.name: Songkhla Old Town Museum
items.blurb: Sits on Nakhon Nai Road and tells the story of Songkhla's trading-port history and local way of life — worth visiting first to give context before you walk the streets

blocks.text: Day 2 — Cross the Bridge to Koh Yo

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Drive across Tinsulanonda Bridge, visit the folklore museum, then eat lakeside seafood

items.activity: Leave your hotel and drive across Tinsulanonda Bridge onto Koh Yo — a small island sitting in the middle of Songkhla Lake
items.note: Tinsulanonda Bridge was once the longest lake-crossing bridge in Thailand · The midspan viewpoint gives a sweeping panorama over the lake

items.activity: Visit the Folklore Museum at the Institute of Southern Thai Studies — traditional southern Thai objects and ways of life displayed inside Thai-style wooden buildings on a hillside
items.note: Adult THB 50, child THB 10 · The grounds are spacious and easy to explore, with great lake views from the hilltop

items.activity: Lunch at a waterfront restaurant on Koh Yo — order snapper from the lake, shrimp, crab, and fresh seafood dishes while sitting right on the water
items.note: Popular spots on the island include Nam Khiang Din, The Lagoon, and several other waterside seafood houses · Weekends get crowded — call ahead to book a water-view table

items.activity: Drive a loop around the island, stopping at fruit orchards, Koh Yo woven-fabric shops, and lake viewpoints along the way
items.note: Koh Yo hand-woven fabric is the island's signature craft — good for souvenirs · The whole island is small enough to circle in one afternoon

items.activity: Head back to the Songkhla side and stop for a coffee or a rest before deciding where to eat dinner
items.note: If you still want more of the old town, the Nang Ngam area comes alive in the evening — go back and catch whatever you missed yesterday

blocks.title: Koh Yo Tip
blocks.html: Koh Yo's waterfront seafood restaurants fill up fast on weekends and waterside tables with views go first. Call ahead or arrive before noon to secure a good spot. Seafood here is priced by weight — ask the price per kilogram before you order so the bill doesn't catch you off guard.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Eat and Shop Hat Yai Before You Fly

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Check out, move to Hat Yai, eat dim sum, ride the cable car, then shop Kim Yong Market

items.activity: Check out, drive from Songkhla into Hat Yai, and kick off the morning with dim sum at one of the city's famous spots
items.note: Dim sum is Hat Yai's staple breakfast · Chok Dee Tae Tiam opens at 06:00–11:30 on Lammai Songkhrao Road — it's busy so take a number and pick items off the trolleys

items.activity: Visit Hat Yai Public Park and ride the cable car up the hill for city views, then visit the temple at the summit
items.note: Hat Yai's cable car was the first aerial tramway in Thailand · Check the operating schedule before going — it closes periodically for maintenance

items.activity: Lunch in Hat Yai — try the crispy Hat Yai fried chicken or old-school khao man gai (Hainanese chicken rice) at a long-running city spot
items.note: Hat Yai fried chicken is marinated in spices, deep-fried until crunchy, and topped with crispy shallots — you'll find it at stalls throughout the market areas

items.activity: Stock up on souvenirs at Kim Yong Market — dried goods, imported snacks, cashews, and southern Thai treats all under one roof
items.note: Kim Yong Market is open daily 06:00–18:00 on Niphat Uthit 3 Road · There's some room to bargain, and buying several items often gets you a freebie

items.activity: Pick up any last snacks, make a final souvenir run, then head out to Hat Yai International Airport
items.note: Allow at least 1.5–2 hrs before your flight · Hat Yai city centre to the airport is around 20–30 min

blocks.text: Must-Eat Picks for the Whole Trip

items.name: Hat Yai Dim Sum — Chok Dee Tae Tiam
items.blurb: Generously stuffed dumplings that Hat Yai locals have been lining up for years — pair with a bowl of hot bak kut teh. Take a number, then pick pieces straight off the trolleys.
items.meta: Breakfast · Lammai Songkhrao Rd, Hat Yai · Open 06:00–11:30

items.name: Koh Yo Lakeside Seafood
items.blurb: Songkhla Lake snapper, shrimp, crab, and shellfish pulled fresh from the water — eat it right on the shore with a breeze coming off the lake. Nam Khiang Din and The Lagoon both have great waterside tables.
items.meta: Lunch/Dinner · Koh Yo · Priced by weight

items.name: Hat Yai Fried Chicken
items.blurb: Spice-marinated chicken fried until deeply golden, finished with crispy fried shallots on top — Hat Yai's most iconic snack. Eat it plain or with sticky rice.

items.name: Clay-Pot Ice Cream, Nang Ngam Road
items.blurb: An old-school coconut ice cream shop on Nang Ngam Road that scoops straight from chilled clay pots — the old-town signature that everyone stops for.
items.meta: Dessert · Nang Ngam Rd, Songkhla Old Town

items.name: Pa Mol's Charcoal Egg Cakes
items.blurb: Traditional Songkhla egg cakes baked over charcoal with a buttery filling — the aroma alone pulls you in, and they taste best eaten warm right in front of the stall.
items.meta: Snack · Nang Ngam Rd, Songkhla Old Town

items.name: Songkhla-Style Stew Rice (Khao Stew, beef/pork)
items.blurb: Rice topped with a Songkhla-style braised stew — the rich broth is easy to sip and the meat is fall-apart tender. Locals have been eating this for breakfast and lunch for generations.

items.name: Tao Khua Songkhla
items.blurb: A local Songkhla salad bowl with rice noodles, fried tofu, boiled egg, and vegetables — all dressed in a tangy-sweet sauce with a distinctly southern kick.

items.name: Kim Yong Market Souvenirs, Hat Yai
items.blurb: Cashews, macadamias, imported snacks, dried goods, and southern Thai treats — all in one market. Buy a few things and you'll usually get extras thrown in.
items.meta: Souvenirs · Niphat Uthit 3 Rd, Hat Yai · Open 06:00–18:00

items: Entry fees — Khao Tang Kuan elevator THB 30, Koh Yo Folklore Museum THB 50, Hat Yai cable car charged separately. Total entry costs for the whole trip are well under THB 200/person.

Transport — Renting a car at around THB 800–1,200/day is the most flexible option since sights are spread across three zones. If you'd rather not drive, hiring a daily taxi or minivan is a straightforward alternative.

Accommodation — Guesthouses in Songkhla old town start from a few hundred baht and go up to around THB 1,000+/night. Hat Yai hotels near the market area cover all price levels. Choose based on which zone you want to wake up in.
Souvenirs — Dried goods and snacks from Kim Yong Market, Koh Yo woven fabric, and old-town sweets. Buy on the last day so everything stays fresh and easy to pack.

faq.q: How many days do you need for Songkhla and Hat Yai?
faq.a: Three days and two nights is the sweet spot if you want to cover Songkhla old town, Koh Yo, and Hat Yai without rushing — the attractions are spread across different zones. One day is possible but you'll have to pick a single zone, such as just the old town and Samila Beach.

faq.q: How far apart are Songkhla and Hat Yai, and how do you get between them?
faq.a: About 30 km — roughly 30–40 minutes by car. Minivans, shared songthaews, and taxis run between the two cities, but renting a car gives you the most freedom since the sights are spread across multiple spots.

faq.q: What is there to do on Koh Yo, and do you need a boat?
faq.a: No boat needed — Tinsulanonda Bridge connects the island directly to the mainland, so you drive straight on. Once there you have the Folklore Museum, lakeside seafood restaurants, Koh Yo woven-fabric shops, and scenic viewpoints. Half a day to a full day is enough to see it all.

faq.q: Should I stay in Songkhla or Hat Yai after landing at Hat Yai Airport?
faq.a: If old-town walking and the sea are your priority, base in Songkhla. If shopping and easy airport access matter more, stay in Hat Yai. This itinerary suggests two nights in Songkhla and one final night in Hat Yai so you're close to the airport on departure day.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit Songkhla?
faq.a: February through August tends to be drier with comfortable weather. October to December is the rainy season on this side of the Gulf, with frequent downpours — if you visit then, build in some indoor backup options like museums and cafés.
